data.name: Zeit²
data.detailed_description:
Zeit²™ is a traditional side-scrolling, 2D, shoot-’em-up game that brings unprecedented elements to the game experience. Zeit²’s unique time travel feature has yet to be seen in this genre even after decades of great games.
Intuitive controls allow players to move forward and backward in time making it possible for the player to combine shots and power, and even be assisted by a shadow version of yourself. Blast away swarms of enemies, get the highest score and discover how you can assist yourself in new exciting ways by warping time at will.

Key Features

  • Time Travel: Assist yourself and perform stunning moves by interacting with your time shadow when travelling back in time. Pace the game and gain extra points by speeding up time. Balance your time travel and life energy to master the game through 70 challenges.
  • 8 Epic Bosses Battles: Discover the potential of your arsenal of powerful moves while fighting over a dozen different enemies and defeating the eight massive bosses.
  • Weapon Upgrades: Your main weapon can be upgraded three times and you will feel the striking force of your additional weapon systems including Beam-Shot, Chain-Shot and Shockwave. The bonus system gives you extra score multipliers as long as you don’t miss out on shooting all enemies.
  • 6 Challenging Game Modes: Go on a journey through 20 chapters of action and variety in the Arcade mode. Challenge others for the highest score in the other modes: Score Attack, Survival, Wave, Time Limit and Tactics. All modes are well integrated with leaderboards and unlockable achievements.
  • Easily accessible for the casual player and yet challenging for the hardcore gamer.

pc_requirements.minimum:
• OS *: Originally released for Windows 7, the game can be played on Windows 10 and Windows 11 OS
  • Processor: at least 2.13 Ghz Intel Core 2 Duo or equivalent
  • Memory: 2GB
  • Graphics: at least Geforce 79XX or equivalent with DirectX 9, Shader Model 3.0, 256 MB VRAM, VGA resolution
  • DirectX®: DirectX 9
  • Hard Drive: 1 GB free disk space

reviews.review:
Zeit² takes the familiar side-scrolling shoot ’em up formula and reshapes it around an inventive time-manipulation system. Developed by Brightside Games and published by Ubisoft, the game combines traditional arcade shooting with mechanics that encourage planning, experimentation, and careful resource management. Rather than relying entirely on quick reflexes and memorizing enemy patterns, it asks players to consider how actions performed in the past can influence what happens next.

The defining feature is the ability to manipulate time while fighting. Players can rewind events, effectively returning to an earlier moment while creating a shadow of their previous actions. This allows the player to cooperate with their own past performance, producing overlapping attacks and opening tactical possibilities that would be impossible in a conventional shooter. Rewinding is therefore much more than a convenient way of correcting mistakes. Learning how to use previous actions offensively becomes an important part of mastering the game.

Time can also be accelerated, creating another layer of risk and reward. Moving quickly through manageable situations can improve efficiency and contribute to stronger scoring opportunities, while careless use of temporal abilities can leave the player poorly prepared for tougher encounters. Because health and time-related resources must be considered together, constantly reversing mistakes is not necessarily the best strategy. The game becomes increasingly satisfying once the player stops treating time travel as an emergency feature and begins incorporating it naturally into combat.

Its shooting mechanics provide enough variety to complement this central idea. The main weapon can be improved, while abilities such as Beam-Shot, Chain-Shot, and Shockwave offer additional ways of handling different enemy formations. More than a dozen enemy types appear throughout the experience, along with eight bosses that provide larger tests of movement, weapon use, and time manipulation. Some encounters can become hectic, but the ability to reconsider previous actions gives combat a distinctly tactical quality.

The main Arcade experience contains 20 chapters, but the game provides several additional modes for players interested in mastering its systems. Score Attack encourages optimization and aggressive play, Survival focuses on endurance, Wave challenges players with sustained enemy pressure, Time Limit emphasizes speed, and Tactics places greater importance on understanding the underlying mechanics. There are also 70 challenges, extensive statistics, leaderboards, and 70 Steam achievements. These features make replayability one of the game's stronger qualities, particularly for players who enjoy improving scores and refining strategies.

Presentation is relatively modest compared with modern shooters, but the visual design generally prioritizes clarity. Enemies, projectiles, effects, and the player's ship remain readable during most encounters, which is especially important when temporal mechanics already demand considerable attention. The graphics inevitably show their age, yet the straightforward presentation works reasonably well with the arcade structure. The real attraction has always been the unusual gameplay concept rather than elaborate environments or cinematic spectacle.

The learning curve is handled reasonably well because the basic shooting controls are immediately recognizable. Moving, firing, and avoiding threats feel familiar, while the complexity gradually emerges from understanding when and why to manipulate time. Casual players can concentrate on surviving the stages, whereas dedicated players can pursue multipliers, eliminate every available target, experiment with time acceleration, and search for increasingly efficient solutions. This gives the game a welcome difference between simply completing content and genuinely mastering it.

Its limitations are mostly connected to its age and specialized design. The campaign is not intended to provide an expansive story-driven adventure, and much of the long-term value depends on whether the player enjoys replaying stages, improving scores, completing challenges, and collecting achievements. The original PC release also carries some legacy baggage that feels increasingly dated. Players primarily interested in modern progression systems or extensive narrative content may consequently find the overall package comparatively narrow.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently best regarded as Unverified rather than officially Steam Deck Verified or Playable. Its relatively modest hardware requirements make the underlying game a reasonable candidate for portable play, but the lack of an official compatibility rating means functionality should not be assumed to be completely trouble-free. Controller behavior, compatibility layers, or other configuration details may require additional attention depending on the current SteamOS environment.

Zeit² remains memorable because its time mechanics genuinely alter how a shoot ’em up can be played. Rewinding, cooperating with previous actions, accelerating time, managing resources, and chasing score multipliers create a surprisingly thoughtful arcade experience beneath its simple exterior. The graphics and overall presentation belong unmistakably to an earlier era, but the underlying design still has originality. For players who enjoy arcade shooters with experimental mechanics and plenty of opportunities for score chasing, it offers a compact but unusually creative challenge.

Rating: 7/10
